chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Imran al-Shafa, from Rabi' ibn Abdullah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah al-Basri, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorced his wife while she was pregnant, and there were two (fetuses) in her womb. She gave birth to one, and one remained. He said: The divorce is established by the first one, and she is not permissible for the husbands until she gives birth to what is in her womb.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce for a pregnant woman carrying twins?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanics of *iddah* for a polytocous pregnancy, establishing that the divorce is finalized upon the first birth while the waiting period extends to the second. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the physical state of pregnancy dictates the duration of the waiting period, ensuring clarity in lineage and marital status. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how multiple births are handled in Islamic family law.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Ali Bin Imran Sl Shafa, from Rabie Bin Abdullah, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah Al Basry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who divorced his wife and she was pregnant, and in her belly were two (twins). So she placed one, and there remained one’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is proved by the first one, and she is not Permissible for the marriage until she places what is in her belly’.
en.sarwar: 10. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ja‘far ibn Sama’ah from Ali ‘Imran al-Shifa’ from Rib‘iy ibn ‘ Abd Allah from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah al-Basriy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who divorces his pregnant wife with two children in her womb. She gives birth to one and one remains. He (the Imam) said, ‘She becomes stranger with the birth of one child and she is not lawful for marriage until the birth of the other child.’
